title: Container Shipping Demurrage & Detention Disputes: Discourse Markers in Commercial Dispute Escalation
description: Advanced commercial purchasing module evaluating container shipping demurrage & detention disputes: discourse markers in commercial dispute escalation.
learning_objectives: Master professional Formal Discourse Markers (notwithstanding, conversely) in wholesale food procurement
Eliminate common Czech interference errors in container shipping demurrage & detention disputes: discourse markers in commercial dispute escalation
Demonstrate precision in international commercial negotiations and food safety documentation

questions.prompt: _____ earlier during simulation, the catastrophic breakdown of the refrigerated container cold-chain data logger would have been avoided.

options.text: If the engineers detected the defect
Had the engineers detected the defect
Would the engineers have detected the defect
Did the engineers detect the defect

explanations.correct: Inverted Third Conditional 'Had the engineers detected...' correctly replaces 'If the engineers had detected...' in formal engineering discourse.
explanations.wrong_A: 'If the engineers detected' is Second Conditional (hypothetical present/future), incompatible with past 'would have been avoided'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'Would... have' cannot appear inside the conditional premise clause.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Did... detect' expresses a past question, not an unreal conditional condition.

questions.cz_learning_point: Ve formální technické angličtině se podmínka v minulosti často tvoří inverzí bez 'if': 'Had the engineers detected...' = 'Kdyby bývali inženýři zjistili...'. Do podmínky nikdy nepatří *would*.

questions.prompt: Under no circumstances _____ the secondary safety interlocks during live machine operation.

explanations.correct: Negative phrase 'Under no circumstances' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: 'should technicians bypass'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'technicians should bypass' lacks required subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanations.wrong_B: 'must to' is ungrammatical; modal 'must' does not take 'to'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Záporné úvodní fráze ('Under no circumstances', 'Rarely', 'Seldom') vyžadují převrácený slovosled (inverzi jako u otázky): 'Under no circumstances should technicians bypass...'.

questions.prompt: If the preventative maintenance had been carried out properly last week, the system _____ erratic readings today.

explanations.correct: Mixed conditional: past unreal action ('had been carried out last week') with ongoing present result ('today') takes 'would not be showing'.
explanations.wrong_B: 'would not have shown' refers purely to past consequence, but adverbial 'today' anchors the result to the present.
explanations.wrong_C: 'will not show' is First Conditional, incompatible with past counterfactual condition.
explanations.wrong_D: Indicative 'does not show' cannot express hypothetical consequence.

questions.cz_learning_point: Smíšený kondicionál (Mixed Conditional): minulá příčina spojená s přítomným následkem: 'If it had been done [minulost], it would not be showing [dnes]'.

questions.prompt: Quality audit directives mandate that every facility _____ compliance with EU Regulation 178/2002 general food law without exception.

explanations.correct: Mandative subjunctive after 'mandate that' requires the base verb form 'demonstrate' regardless of singular subject.
explanations.wrong_A: Indicative 'demonstrates' with 3rd person -s violates mandative subjunctive syntax.
explanations.wrong_B: Future 'will demonstrate' is incorrect after mandative 'mandate that'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Subjunktiv po formálních slovesech požadavku (mandate that, require that, insist that) vyžaduje základní tvar slovesa bez -s i u 3. osoby: 'mandate that every facility demonstrate'.

questions.prompt: _____ comprehensive non-destructive ultrasonic testing, the inspection team cleared the perishable fresh fish consignment lead time for immediate deployment.

explanations.correct: Perfect active participle 'Having completed' correctly expresses an action finished prior to the main clause action 'cleared'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'After completed' is ungrammatical; 'after' requires an '-ing' participle or full clause.
explanations.wrong_B: 'Have completed' cannot act as an introductory participial phrase.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Being completed' is passive present, but the inspection team actively completed the testing.

questions.cz_learning_point: Předpřítomné participium (Having completed = poté, co dokončili) vyjadřuje předcházející děj před hlavní větou.

questions.prompt: _____ severe supply chain bottlenecks, the engineering team delivered the prototype on schedule.

explanations.correct: 'Notwithstanding' is a formal preposition followed by a noun phrase ('severe supply chain bottlenecks').
explanations.wrong_A: 'Although' is a conjunction and must be followed by a full clause with subject and verb.
explanations.wrong_D: 'Whereas' introduces a contrastive clause, not a prepositional phrase.

questions.cz_learning_point: 'Notwithstanding' (navzdory / bez ohledu na) se pojí s podstatným jménem, zatímco spojky jako 'Although' a 'Even though' vyžadují celou větu se slovesem.

questions.prompt: The failure rate of the eco-packaging transport film procurement order is understood _____ by micro-fractures in the mounting alloy.

explanations.correct: Perfect passive infinitive 'to have been caused' correctly attributes a past completed cause to a current condition.
explanations.wrong_A: Present passive 'to be caused' fails to indicate past completion.
explanations.wrong_B: Participle 'having caused' cannot follow passive reporting verb 'is understood'.
explanations.wrong_C: Active infinitive 'to cause' is wrong in voice; failure rates do not cause themselves.

questions.cz_learning_point: Vazba 'is understood to have been caused' (má se za to, že bylo způsobeno) vyjadřuje minulý děj pomocí minulého infinitivu trpného.

questions.prompt: Only after the second calibration cycle _____ the anomalous drift in sensor telemetry.

explanations.correct: Limiting introductory phrase 'Only after...' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion with Past Simple: 'did our technicians notice'.
explanations.wrong_B: 'our technicians noticed' lacks the required subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanations.wrong_C: 'noticed our technicians' is archaic full inversion without auxiliary 'did'.
explanations.wrong_D: Present perfect conflicts with the finished narrative event.

questions.cz_learning_point: Zdůrazňující úvodní vazba 'Only after...' vyžaduje inverzní slovosled s pomocným slovesem: 'Only after the cycle did technicians notice...'.

questions.prompt: Given the rigorous pre-flight inspections, the hydraulic failure _____ occurred without catastrophic external impact.

explanations.correct: 'Cannot possibly have' expresses conclusive deduction of impossibility regarding a past event.
explanations.wrong_A: 'must not have' expresses deduction that something did not happen, but lacks impossibility nuance.
explanations.wrong_B: 'should not have' expresses unmet expectation or reproach, not impossibility.
explanations.wrong_D: 'may not have' expresses mere uncertainty, incompatible with 'conclusive'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Vyjádření naprosté nemožnosti v minulosti: 'cannot possibly have occurred' (rozhodně nemohlo dojít k...).

questions.prompt: The international consortium signed an operational agreement, under the terms of _____ all patent rights remain protected.

explanations.correct: Prepositional relative phrase 'under the terms of which' strictly takes 'which' when referring to an inanimate contract or agreement.
explanations.wrong_A: 'that' cannot follow a preposition in formal relative clauses.
explanations.wrong_D: 'what' cannot function as a relative pronoun with an explicit antecedent.

questions.cz_learning_point: Po předložkách v rozvitých vztažných větách se pro věci a smlouvy používá výhradně 'which': 'under the terms of which' (podle jehož podmínek).
